# Draft:Dolly Gray Children's Literature Award

The Dolly Gray Children's Literature Award recognizes authors, illustrators, and publishers who create books that authentically portray individuals with developmental disabilities. The award is presented by the Council for Exceptional Children (CEC) through its Division on Autism and Developmental Disabilities (DADD).
Established in 2000, the award was created to recognize high-quality children's literature that features characters with developmental disabilities. It is awarded every even-numbered year to the author and illustrator of a picture book and to the author of an intermediate or young adult book.
The award is named after Dolly Sharpe Gray, who was born on September 20, 1971, with severe cerebral palsy. She passed away shortly before her eighteenth birthday due to a respiratory infection. Children's literature played a significant role in Dolly's life. Because she was unable to walk or speak, books allowed her to experience diverse people and places. She especially valued stories that portrayed characters she could identify with. During her lifetime, however, there were very few books that accurately depicted individuals with disabilities. The award was therefore named in her honor to represent the many children with developmental disabilities who wish to see themselves reflected in literature.
Books that receive the Dolly Gray Children's Literature Award have been recognized as valuable resources for teaching multicultural awareness. Literature that authentically portrays individuals with disabilities—such as Dolly Gray Award–winning books—can help foster positive attitudes and behaviors toward people with developmental disabilities. These books have also been recommended for use in bibliotherapy, both to help children learn about individuals with disabilities and to allow children with disabilities to relate to characters who share similar experiences.
The Dolly Gray Children's Literature Award Special Collection is housed at the Harold B. Lee Library at Brigham Young University in Provo. This collection is believed to be the most comprehensive collection of juvenile literature featuring individuals with developmental disabilities.
Additional information about submission guidelines and a complete list of books considered for the award since 2000 can be found on the award's official webpage.

Wikipedia Syntax:
The '''Dolly Gray Children's Literature Award''' is a literary award that recognizes authors, illustrators, and publishers who contribute books that accurately portray individuals with developmental disabilities. The award is given by the Council for Exceptional Children's (CEC) Division on Autism and Developmental Disabilities (DADD).
The award began in 2000 as part of an effort to recognize quality children's literature with characters with developmental disabilities.It is given every even year to an author/illustrator of a picture book and to an author of an intermediate or young adult book.
The award is named after Dolly Sharpe Gray who was born on September 20, 1971, with severe cerebral palsy. She died shortly before her 18th birthday from a respiratory infection. A very important part of life for Dolly was children's literature. Because she was not able to walk or speak, she experienced diverse people and places through literature. She enjoyed books that portrayed characters with whom she could identify. During her time the number of books with accurate depictions of characters with disabilities was limited. The award was named after Dolly Gray to represent the many children with developmental disabilities who want to encounter themselves in literature.
The books that have received the Dolly Gray Children's Literature Award have been recognized as a resource to teach about multiculturality. Using books that have authentic portrayals of individuals with disabilities, such as books that have received the Dolly Gray Award, can help promote positive attitudes and behaviors toward people with developmental disabilities. The award-winning books have also been suggested as tools for bibliotherapy sessions, in order to teach children about others with disabilities, or to have children with disabilities relate to characters with disabilities.
The Dolly Gray Children's Literature Award Special Collection is found at the Harold B. Lee Library at Brigham Young University in Provo, Utah. The collection is likely to be the most complete collection of juvenile literature that includes individuals with developmental disabilities.
More information about the submission guidelines and a full list of books that were considered for the award since the year 2000 can be found at the award's [http://dollygrayaward.com webpage].
